correctness.rationale: Salazar Theorem 4.9 rigorously limits any n>=13 zero at k<=2 to c<=3 and n<=924. Adjoining all primes dividing n preserves k and zero and tightens the applicable c. The equivalence with exact covering of H_n by at most two prime masks (q<=2n) is proved in both directions. The checker exhausts each of the resulting 207 n, reproduces the stored certificate, and directly validates all five supports; it also establishes absence of a one-prime cover at those five inputs. All computations use exact integers. The published analytic cutoff is a stated premise and is not recomputed.

value.rationale: J(2) is an explicitly motivated endpoint in recent number theory research. Determining its exact value 46 and every attainable even zero with this first nontrivial support budget resolves a natural finite-but-global classification, distinguishing one and two noncolliding primes. It is not a random slice: the parameter and its positivity question come from the source, and the table is complete after a rigorous general cutoff.
